label: Hacktoberfest
source: public/data/issues.json.gz (40017 issues across 290 repositories, snapshot 2026-10-21) filtered to issues whose labels read "hacktoberfest", plus gh api search/repositories?q=topic:hacktoberfest&sort=stars
note: One row per repository we can evidence as part of Hacktoberfest - the unit is "Hacktoberfest repositories", because GitHub's topic and a repository's own labels are the only machine-readable signal the program leaves; Hacktoberfest publishes no participant or completion archive, so this is not a list of people who completed it and rows carry no year. 0 row(s) come from GitHub's repository search for the `hacktoberfest` topic (most-starred first) and 6 from this site's own issue snapshot, where 6 of the 290 crawled repositories carry hacktoberfest-labelled issues (0 of those also carry the topic). Stars, language, license, topics, description and the repository URL are the GitHub API response for each repository; where the evidence is our snapshot the row says so in `s` and names the labelled-issue count in `b`. Hacktoberfest's 2022 contribution rules and bot-mitigation limits are documented on github.blog, but no per-project record is published anywhere, which is why this shard is repository-level evidence rather than a project archive.
